brief: How we orchestrate 12 agents in production. Tools, patterns, gotchas.

slots.title: 1. Router, the traffic cop
slots.body: We use a state machine to route requests. It assigns tasks based on intent, not just keywords. This prevents agent collisions.

slots.title: 2. Bus, the nervous system
slots.body: Agents publish events to a Redis stream. Consumers pick up jobs asynchronously. This decouples workloads and keeps latency low.

slots.title: 3. Postgres, the memory bank
slots.body: We store agent state and thread history in PostgreSQL. Row-level locking prevents race conditions when multiple agents update shared context.

slots.title: 4. Docker, the isolation unit
slots.body: Each agent runs in its own container. Resource caps stop one runaway process from starving the fleet. Health checks restart failures fast.

slots.title: 5. Slack, the alert channel
slots.body: We stream structured logs to a dedicated Slack channel. Engineers get paged when error rates spike. Context threads speed up debugging.

slots.title: 6. Prompts, the hidden code
slots.body: Version control your prompts like any other dependency. A single wording drift can break an entire agent pipeline. Regression tests catch this.

slots.headline: Build Your Agent Fleet
slots.subline: Steal our stack and patterns. DM 'stack' for the full architecture doc.
